stories.headline: 2-Deoxyglucose Dendrimer-Enabled Niclosamide Delivery to FRβ-Expressing Macrophages Alleviates Endometriosis Progression and Associated Hyperalgesia
stories.dek: A targeted niclosamide formulation reduced lesion burden and pain-associated behavior in a mouse model; human efficacy remains untested.
tldr: Researchers reported a dendrimer formulation designed to deliver niclosamide to FRβ-expressing macrophages.
In a mouse model, the formulation reduced endometriosis lesion number and volume and improved pain-associated behavior two weeks after treatment.
The result is preclinical; the cited research does not establish safety or efficacy in people.

body.text: The study reports a targeted 2-deoxyglucose dendrimer carrying niclosamide and describes testing in a mouse model of endometriosis. The researchers report reduced lesion number and volume and improved hyperalgesia after treatment.

Nature's coverage identifies the work as a mouse study and notes that replication in people would be needed before it could support a human treatment claim. Phys.org also reports the research as an early-stage, preclinical result.

stories.whyItMatters: The work explores a nonhormonal, targeted delivery approach in a disease area where treatment options remain limited. Its translational significance depends on follow-up evidence in people; the current result is confined to mice.
